DHI.thesis_one_line: America's largest homebuilder, priced for flat-to-low growth, with a strong balance sheet but two straight quarters of cut guidance and shrinking margins.
kill_criteria: Full-year FY2026 consolidated revenue guidance cut a third consecutive time (below the current $32.5-33.0bn range at the Q4 FY26 release, due 2026-10-29)
Home sales gross margin falls below 18.0% for two consecutive quarters (from 20.7% in Q3 FY26)
Homebuilding-segment debt-to-capital exceeds 25% (from 15.4% at 6/30/26), on the homebuilding-only entity basis, not consolidated
Consolidated operating cash flow negative for two consecutive quarters
Homes closed or revenue fall below the low end of the Q3 FY26 guide for two consecutive quarters
key_adverse_facts: Fiscal 2026 consolidated revenue guidance cut from $33.5-34.5bn (Q2 FY26 release, 2026-04-21) to $32.5-33.0bn (Q3 FY26 release, 2026-07-21), a 3.7% cut at the midpoint in one quarter
Company states it expects sales incentives to 'remain elevated during the fourth quarter' (Q3 FY26 release, verbatim), a second consecutive quarter of margin caution
TTM diluted EPS $10.49 is down from FY2025 full-year EPS $11.57 and well below the FY2024 peak of $14.34

Roughly half of consolidated debt ($7,112.6m) sits outside the homebuilding segment ($3,685.3m), mostly at the captive mortgage-finance arm; a consolidated-only leverage read would overstate homebuilding risk
data_conflicts: None material; b1_live_scores' negative earnings-momentum (SUE) reading is consistent with, not contradicted by, the primary-source guidance cuts found in the filings
DHI.confidence_in_thesis: medium (low leverage and strong buyback capacity are well evidenced; near-term margin/volume trajectory is still deteriorating and the reverse DCF reads close to fair value rather than clearly cheap)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for DHI (confirmed absent from v1_valuation_table.csv and v1_valuation.json); the analyst's own reverse DCF (implied 10-yr FCF CAGR ~0.9-1.8% at 9.0-9.5% WACC) is read as in_line with a 2-4%/yr base case, not clearly below it, given TTM FCF sits above a full-cycle trough.

scenario_returns_3y.scenario_basis: TTM EPS $10.49, 13.5x trailing P/E; bear = further margin/volume decline to ~11x on flat-to-down EPS; base = EPS stabilizes and P/E holds ~13-14x with ~7.5% combined buyback/dividend yield; bull = housing recovery lifts EPS and re-rates to ~16x.

ESS.thesis_one_line: A West Coast apartment landlord in supply-constrained markets, raising its full-year cash-earnings guidance while trading for almost no priced-in growth.
kill_criteria: Full-year 2026 Core FFO/share guidance cut below the current $16.03-$16.25 range at the Q3 2026 release (estimated late October 2026)
Same-property revenue growth falls below 2.0% for two consecutive quarters (from 2.7-2.9% currently)
Estimated net debt/EBITDA rises above 6.5x (analyst estimate; company does not disclose an exact ratio)
California or Washington state/local rent-control legislation caps annual same-property revenue growth below 2% system-wide
Dividend increase streak broken (would end the 32-consecutive-year record cited by the company)
key_adverse_facts: Full-year 2026 GAAP net income per diluted share guidance midpoint was cut $0.29 (to $5.58) in the same Q2 2026 release that raised Core FFO guidance +$0.20 (to $16.14) -- a real GAAP-vs-adjusted divergence, not simply reconciled line-by-line at this depth
GAAP diluted EPS fell sharply quarter over quarter ($1.65 in Q1 2026 to $0.97 in Q2 2026) even as Core FFO and same-property NOI both grew
Concentrated in three states (California, Washington) with above-average rent-regulation risk
Estimated net debt/EBITDA of ~5.4-5.8x is an analyst estimate, not a company-disclosed figure; no exact ratio was found in the two releases reviewed
data_conflicts: b1_live_scores' weak earnings-momentum (SUE) score for ESS looks like a REIT-specific artefact: GAAP EPS is lumpy from non-cash items and disposition-gain timing that the SUE calculation is not built to normalize for a REIT whose targeted metric is Core FFO, not GAAP EPS
ESS.confidence_in_thesis: medium (Core FFO raise and same-property re-acceleration are well evidenced from primary sources; leverage estimate and GAAP-vs-Core-FFO gap were not fully decomposed within the time box)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for ESS (confirmed absent from v1_valuation_table.csv and v1_valuation.json); the analyst's own reverse DCF (implied 10-yr Core FFO/share CAGR ~0% to +1.2% at 7.5-8.0% cost of equity) is below a 3-4%/yr base case for a supply-constrained coastal apartment REIT with a 32-year dividend-growth record.

scenario_returns_3y.scenario_basis: FY26 guided Core FFO/share midpoint $16.14, ~16.8x P/Core FFO plus ~3.5-4% dividend yield; bear = same-property growth stalls near 0%, multiple compresses to ~15x; base = 2-3%/yr Core FFO growth at a steady ~16-17x multiple plus the dividend; bull = supply tightens further, Core FFO growth accelerates to 4-5%/yr with modest re-rating.

EXR.thesis_one_line: The second-largest US self-storage operator, just turning same-store growth positive after a multi-year supply glut, priced for almost no further growth.
kill_criteria: Full-year 2026 Core FFO/share guidance cut below the current $8.25-$8.40 range at the Q3 2026 release (estimated late October 2026)
Same-store NOI growth guidance reversed back to negative territory (from the current 0.50%-2.50% full-year range)
Same-store occupancy falls below 93.0% for two consecutive quarters (from 94.2% at 6/30/26)
Estimated net debt/EBITDA rises above 6.5x (analyst estimate; company does not disclose a single total-debt figure)
Third-party-managed store count declines quarter over quarter (from +67 gross / +48 net stores added in Q2 2026)
key_adverse_facts: Same-store occupancy of 94.2% (Q2 2026) is down 20bps year over year even as revenue/NOI improved -- the recovery is being driven by rate, not volume

EXR discontinued the standard XBRL 'NotesPayable' total-debt tag after Q3 2021; total consolidated debt (~$13.65bn at 6/30/26) had to be hand-assembled from the balance sheet's secured/unsecured/revolver line items rather than read from one machine-readable figure -- a disclosure-quality flag
Estimated net debt/EBITDA of ~5.2-5.4x is an analyst estimate, not a company-disclosed figure
Weighted-average one-month SOFR guidance assumption of 3.73% means the FY26 Core FFO guide has embedded floating-rate sensitivity that a rate spike would work against
data_conflicts: b1_live_scores shows a missing (NaN) leverage percentile for EXR; the model's quality score should not be read as having cleared a leverage screen for this name
EXR.confidence_in_thesis: medium (the guidance raise and same-store inflection are well evidenced from primary sources; the fundamental recovery is recent and unconfirmed over multiple quarters, and leverage is an analyst estimate)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for EXR (confirmed absent from v1_valuation_table.csv and v1_valuation.json); the analyst's own reverse DCF (implied 10-yr Core FFO/share CAGR ~ -0.6% to +0.6% at 7.5-8.0% cost of equity) is at or modestly below a 2-4%/yr base case tied to the just-turned-positive same-store outlook and continued third-party management growth.

scenario_returns_3y.scenario_basis: FY26 guided Core FFO/share midpoint $8.325, ~16.0x P/Core FFO plus a $1.62/quarter dividend; bear = same-store recovery stalls/reverses, multiple compresses to ~14x; base = same-store NOI growth continues in the 1-3%/yr range plus third-party management fee growth at a steady ~16x multiple plus the dividend; bull = supply glut clears faster than expected, Core FFO growth reaches 4-5%/yr with re-rating toward ~18x.
